Subject: Clarify default retention windows for prompts vs generated outputs

Hi Rachel,

Thanks again for the demo last week. As part of our procurement checklist we need a clear, written summary of Redwood's default log retention policy so we can include it in our security appendix. Specific asks from our side:

- By default, how long are incoming requests (user prompts) retained?
- How long are model-generated outputs (completions/responses) retained?
- Do streamed tokens (intermediate fragments) get stored differently from final outputs?
- Any exceptions where we would retain longer (billing, legal hold, debug artifacts)?
- Can you confirm whether retention is region-specific (we operate in the US and EU) and whether erasure evidence can be provided for contract purposes?

If you can send a short, plain-language summary plus a one-page matrix we can attach to our SOW that'd be ideal.

Appreciate it — Emma
Procurement, BrightBank

Subject: RE: Clarify default retention windows for prompts vs generated outputs

Emma — thanks for the clear list. Looping in Kim and Marissa to confirm the canonical policy and to attach our one-pager. High level answer below while they pull the matrix:

- Default retention (hosted API): requests (raw prompts) are retained for 45 days by default; outputs (final completions) are retained for 90 days by default.
- Streamed/intermediate tokens: buffered fragments are stored transiently to support streaming; they are not indexed and are retained only for the session buffer (up to 24 hours) unless the session is finalized and captured as an artifact.
- Exceptions: billing logs (usage metering) and audit logs are retained for 1 year. Legal holds or subpoena responses may extend retention — we provide erasure evidence on a per-request basis.

We want to make sure the phrasing is contract-ready; Kim/Marissa — can you confirm exact wording and put together the one-page matrix and a short exportable proof-of-deletion statement we can include in the SOW?

Thanks,
Rachel
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Rachel / Marissa — drafting canonical response. Key policy points (for procurement language):

1) Default capture windows (hosted):
   - Incoming requests (raw prompts, user input): retained by default for 45 days. Purpose: debugging, quality regression detection, and prompt-eval correlation.
   - Model-generated outputs (finalized completions): retained by default for 90 days. Purpose: customer-facing audit, quality monitoring, and billing validation.

2) Streaming / session buffers:
   - Streamed token fragments are treated as ephemeral session buffers. They are kept only to reconstruct the streamed response and are flushed after session end; default buffer TTL is 24 hours. These are not part of the indexed request/response archive.

3) Caching artifacts (KV cache, prefix caches):
   - KV caches are ephemeral and tied to instance lifecycle. Default retention is 7 days for cache metadata; content that contributes to long-term artifacts only persists if explicitly captured.

4) Audit / billing / operational logs:
   - Separate retention policy of 1 year to support billing reconciliations and SLA investigations.

5) Exceptions & legal holds:
   - Legal hold or compliance investigations can extend retention; Redwood provides exportable proof-of-deletion and erasure logs for individual data subject requests or contractually scoped erasures.

6) Residency differences:
   - Data is stored in region selected at provisioning (US, EU). Default retention windows above apply per-region. For EU-hosted instances, we support EU-only storage and will provide erasure evidence within the EU region.

7) Evidence artifacts we can provide:
   - Deletion confirmation token (unique id + timestamp), deletion runbook steps, and a signed export (PDF) showing item ids removed.

8) Contract language suggestion (short):
   - "Redwood Inference will retain customer-generated requests for 45 days and finalized model outputs for 90 days by default. Streamed tokens are ephemeral (up to 24 hours) and separate operational logs are retained for up to 1 year. Redwood will provide deletion evidence and accommodate contractual retention/exemption requests under mutually agreed SOW terms."

I attached a draft retention matrix (retention_matrix_v2.xlsx) and a short external-facing PDF we usually share (redwood-retention-summary.pdf). Jonas, please flag if there are any compliance blockers for BrightBank's EU operations.

-kim
Chief Compliance Officer, Redwood Inference

Emma — attaching the one-page summary and a formal matrix as requested. Below is a concise version you can paste into the SOW.

Concise summary for SOW:
- Requests (prompts): retained by default for 45 days.
- Finalized outputs (completions): retained by default for 90 days.
- Streamed/intermediate tokens: ephemeral, retained up to 24 hours for session reconstruction only.
- Billing/audit logs: retained for 1 year.
- Residency: data stored in the region you select at provisioning; EU-only storage options available for EU customers.
- Erasure evidence: Redwood will provide a deletion confirmation token and a signed PDF showing eradicated item ids for contracted erasure requests.

If you'd like, we can convert the short summary into a single-sentence clause (Kim's suggested language) and add it to the SOW appendix. Please confirm and let me know whether BrightBank needs EU-only storage for this contract.

Thanks — Rachel
